summary: A small computer program, rather than tests on people, calculated a high liver risk score of 93 and a low heart risk score of 25 for Sulfaphenazole [M]. Several similar medicines have been withdrawn from use due to various safety issues [3][4][5]. For example, the related drug Sulfathiazole was pulled from the market in the United States and two other countries because of kidney damage (nephrotoxicity), liver damage, and skin problems (dermatological harm) [3]. Another similar drug called Sulfacarbamide was removed from the market in Germany due to liver harm and blood disorders (hematological harm), while Sulfamethazine was also taken off the market in Germany [4][5].
